quest.title: One There Was, Who Hunted the Moon
quest.description: With The Damselette, you not only uncover surprising truths from your memories but also learn the true identity of the phantom masquerading as your sibling. He may well be one of the Five Sinners Dainsleif once mentioned — Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Primogem x30, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act II
chapter.title: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight

talks.objective: Return to see Lauma and share your new intel

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You relate the gist of your conversation with The Damselette to Lauma (without the Moon Goddess joke.)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The Rächer of Solnari... I've never heard that name before.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let's keep this news confidential for the time being. It would only cause even more panic amongst the people of Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But if this Rerir is as you describe, he will be a truly formidable opponent if we try to take him on by our strength alone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Things might be okay if everyone was willing to work together, but right now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If we don't stick together, we'll be picked off one by one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! Whatever the case, let's start by telling those we can get to join up about the crisis!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As it happens, we have our own reasons to protect Nod-Krai... But even if we didn't, we'd never leave people in the lurch. That ain't our style!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you. The Frostmoon Scions will stand with you to prevent this crisis as best we can.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In addition... I believe that the relationships between the various factions in this land are not cast in stone.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The winds of change are blowing, and we Scions have nowhere to run. Our faith, our sect... all of it is here.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Whether our foe is the Fatui or this Rächer, we must stand our ground and remain true to ourselves, even to the last.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Speaking of allies, the Krumkake Craftshop is the closest by, right? Ineffa's sure to help us!

talks.objective: Contact Aino and Ineffa

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Friendly approach detected. We meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Listen, listen, we've got updates on the Wild Hunt situation!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Mmhmm, mmhmm...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Threat level... exceeds expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Pfftooey! Doesn't matter if he's the Rächer of Solnari, or Solari, or whatever. One volley from my cannon and he'll be blown to smithereens!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: You were there when we fired it, right? If that isn't the kind of firepower that helps you sleep at night, I don't know what is!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: True, but the cannon only works against shambling monsters, right? What if Rerir's super fast?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Well... We'll just get Ineffa to go grab him and tie him down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not taking this seriously at all, are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Anyways... Firepower's not a concern. See those canisters over there? That's all concentrated kuuvahki, which we'll be shipping to Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: More than enough ammo in there to blast that Fatui research facility to bits in a single shot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... sure have been looking forward to this battle, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Of course! This is gonna be the shot that shocks the world! All Nod-Krai — heck, all of Snezhnaya — will know my name once we're through!

choices.text: In that case, our firepower needs are in your hands.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Sure. Travel safe!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Aino, there remains intel left unshared.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Ohhh, right, yeah... Since you're investigating the Wild Hunt, something pretty weird's happened in Nasha Town. Should probably watch out for that once you're back.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Remember that Sousi guy, the Ratnik in charge of firing the cannon? He's... been found dead in their organization's offices.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what!? Didn't we just see him like... half a day ago?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Yeah. It's still new news, so not many people are in the know. We were only informed because we'd worked together closely... and even then, only just now.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: I'll send Ineffa over to Nasha Town with some flowers later... *sigh*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He seemed like a good guy. Didn't put on any airs despite being a superior officer, either.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: The data concurs. This gentleman appears to have been one of the most accomplished amongst the Lightkeepers' Sergeant Majors.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: His character has also received commendation. Most would have lacked the motivation to fatally attack him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That makes it even worse...

choices.text: Could it have been the Wild Hunt?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Hey! What do you mean "actually"?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Either way, I'm not clued in on the details. Only Ratniki have been allowed on-site to investigate the scene. You'll have to find some way in if you want to check it out for yourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it. Let's go, then. You coming along, Ineffa?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: My tasks are incomplete. The last few batches of ammunition must be randomly inspected. You go ahead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, we'll see you later!

choices.text: Is Rerir actually afraid of the cannon?
We'll continue to monitor the Wild Hunt's movements.

talks.objective: Go check on the Lightkeepers

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This must be it. Doesn't look like there's any chance of us getting in with that Ratnik guarding the door, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Should we go speak to the guard first?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Might as well try squeezing blood from a stone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!? Nefer! When did you...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I came over to take a look as soon as I received the news just now. Aino told you about this, then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, while we were passing by the Krumkake Craftshop.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Before we start, shall we see if we've made the same guess?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like the Wild Hunt is on the move.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Indeed. Quicker than we thought, as well.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Keep your eyes peeled for any clues once we get in. No need to jump to conclusions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, but how are we supposed to get in at all?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Just follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Zvoni
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but we're not open to guests right now.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: Sorry about that. They're here to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Zvoni
dialogues.text: ...All of them?

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: The paperwork checks out.

dialogues.speaker: Zvoni
dialogues.text: Alright then, enter.

talks.objective: Enter the crime scene to begin investigating

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: On the way upstairs to the crime scene, you briefly relate the information about the Rächer of Solnari to Nefer...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Paimon might've said this before, Nefer, but you sure do come prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sieciech, my old friend — fill us in, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: Greetings. If you would allow me...

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: The murder happened not long ago. The Sergeant Major was killed by a single piercing strike from a polearm. We have performed a preliminary sweep of the crime scene to facilitate investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: No obvious signs of a violent struggle, no damaged doors or windows. The culprit must have used some other means to enter the room unopposed before performing the deed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Entering unopposed... So, do you think there's a chance that the culprit would usually have right of entry?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(It could have been Rerir in disguise, like how he turned into {M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...)

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: At the moment, the most valuable lead we have is based on an eyewitness report from a nearby resident.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: Specifically, that Flins was seen entering and leaving this place in the time period when the crime most likely occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fl—Flins!?

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: We have tried to contact him, but he has not replied.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Very odd indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... He's the prime suspect right now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'm not particularly inclined to believe that this was an inside job. Flins can come across a bit eccentric, but he does well in missions on the whole.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: He also had no disagreements with the Sergeant Major that we know of, so he lacks a motive to commit such a terrible crime.

dialogues.speaker: Sieciech
dialogues.text: But neither the eyewitness report nor the nature of the fatal wound itself are in his favor... So we are looking for him at present.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Looks like there's not much else to dig up here. Let's go outside and discuss what we've seen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Agreed.

talks.objective: Synthesize the clues you presently have

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, the evidence points to Flins, and he just so happens to have disappeared without a trace. A sticky situation indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We know that this "Flins" could have been Rerir in disguise, but we lack the evidence to prove this to anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Furthermore, Flins has left us with many questions, all of which will require a reasonable explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. He said he would report back to headquarters, but it seems he hasn't gone at all. What could he be doing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The first time I met Flins, I did notice that there was something odd about his lantern... Some power concealed within it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Now that I think about it, that power was somewhat similar to Abyssal energies I've encountered before...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (In the worst case scenario, "Flins" might be an entirely fabricated entity...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's approach the issue this way. First, we must determine our culprit. Was it Flins? Or Rerir in disguise?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's got to be the latter...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. What reason would Flins have to murder Sousi anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: None, as far as I know. And even if he had a motive, it would have been easier to do so out in the wild, rather than in Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, they would have often gone out on missions together — plenty of chances there.

choices.text: Even if it were Rerir, though...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Yes, but there's one thing worth noting here. Remember the intel we got back at the tavern? No one has ever seen a phantom that can take the form of other humans within the Wild Hunt.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: This means that he has been hesitant to abuse this ability, or allow it to become common knowledge... Likely so that he could act in secret under other guises.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But no matter what, borrowing identities comes with risks, right? What if you bump into the person you're imitating along the way?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Precisely. In other words, his goal must have been worth the risk — similar to how he came in disguise to obtain the Moon Marrow.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: He likely knew, then, that the real Flins would not appear and get in his way during this time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And why was he able to determine that?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: We'd have to ask Flins ourselves, I'm afraid. But we shouldn't jump to any conclusions here. We can't discount the possibility that he might actually be the murderer himself — not yet, at least.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And there are other, less likely scenarios — for instance, Rerir may have already killed Flins long ago, and been living as him for some time now...

choices.text: Regardless...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Yes. That is our ticket to a breakthrough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we've got to find him before the Lightkeepers do, or we might never see him again...!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Steady now. Our friend should be back soon.

response.speaker: Sieciech
response.text: We've tracked him down — to a beach north of Nasha Town. The Wild Hunt is present too, so we're putting a force together.

response.speaker: Sieciech
response.text: ...I'll have you know that this is top-secret information I'm leaking here.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Don't worry. You'll receive a top-class reward in return.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The beach is all yours. I'll stay and slow the Lightkeepers down — things might go south if you bump into one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, before we go! Should we reveal Rerir's secret?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since he's trying to keep it all hush-hush, why don't we just pull the curtains on his little trick? That'll teach him to sneak around pretending to be other people!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Why are you laughing?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh, I was just imagining how satisfying that would feel... But I'm afraid this revelation would only stir up more chaos.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Setting aside the matter of evidence, some may trust Flins on our account, whereas others would suspect him on account of his behavior.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Tossing him into a swirling tumult of public opinion like that might just give Rerir more opportunities to capitalize on.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And think about it — once people learn that he can masquerade as those they trust, would they continue to welcome friends into their homes with such open hearts?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Unease grips the hearts of those in Nasha Town already. We should avoid throwing more fuel onto the fire.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Yeah, you're right. You've really thought of everything, huh? Nothing for it, then. We've just gotta find Flins!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Indeed. But just in case, let me stress once more — we should neither be excessively afraid of "Rerir," nor trust in "Flins" too lightly.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: This light source is of special Lightkeeper design. It provides illumination within Wild Hunt anomalies, and can briefly dispel the Abyssal fog within.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right, we'll have to deal with that mess too... Yeah, this'll be important. Thanks a bunch, Nefer!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You're welcome. I've charged it to your account, by the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you—

choices.text: We have to find him.
His motives would be just as unclear.

talks.objective: Go to where the Wild Hunt has emerged

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Best let her rest.

talks.objective: Investigate the Wild Hunt phenomenon further

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The wind blows stronger. May your path ahead be smooth.

talks.objective: Investigate the Wild Hunt phenomenon further
Defeat the monsters before you

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This monster was lurking near the lamp... that must've been a planned ambush. We're not falling for that again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? There's something inside it, some small device...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Why isn't it giving off light anymore? Is it broken? We'd better take it with us.

talks.objective: Proceed deeper within to investigate
Proceed deeper within to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Zvoni
dialogues.text: For now, please keep the current situation confidential.

talks.objective: Follow the trail on the ground
Use the lantern's light to pass through the Phantasmal Zone

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Batch inspection complete. Approved. Next up...

talks.objective: Help Flins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you were tangling with Rerir out here, all by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: So... That vile phantom hiding inside the Wild Hunt has a name of his own— Argh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's find a spot to rest first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you don't look so good...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: ...Sorry you had to see me like this. All the same, you have my sincere thanks for your aid.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: To think you had the power to so easily cleanse the filth staining the lantern, which tormented me so...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Might I ask what magic that was, or whose pupil you are? I believe I might have saved some face had I mastered just a fraction of such abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't understand it either. Just my constitution, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And an enviable constitution it is. A pity that such abilities cannot be acquired.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did Abyssal power just burst out of your lantern, anyway...?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That is a long story. Many moons ago, when on Wild Hunt clearance duty, I shattered one of its cores, only for a special crystalline object to fall out.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I sensed a power surging within it that was at once familiar yet strangely illusory...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I freely confess to being an avid collector of ancient gems, coins, and other curios. And curiosity it was that had me store this crystal inside my lantern.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Afterwards, I wound up collecting a few more such crystals quite by accident, and discovered that they could merge into a single piece without my prompting... Though my understanding ends there.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It was only recently that they began slowly emitting Abyssal energy, which could neither be dispelled nor weakened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that what Rerir claimed belonged to him? That must be what he's after, then.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I concur. And here's the kicker... Before, he was exceedingly weak. In fact, I've already beaten him several times, though I could not destroy him completely.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But I noticed while engaging him that the crystal fragment would restrict my powers. As such, it occurred to me that I should hide it rather than tangle with him any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Alas, he has proved most fixated upon this fragment, and for some reason, his strength has grown by leaps and bounds since I last encountered him.

choices.text: If this object is contaminated by the Abyss...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And where, might I ask, would it be safe? Or do you think it wiser I threw it away?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Were our places switched, would you discard it, knowing that its perilous might was beyond your ability to counteract, yet capable of causing greater harm should it lie beyond your grasp?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Throwing it away would mean giving the bad guy what he wants! But exposing yourself to its corrosion and growing weaker by the day... That sounds super dangerous, too...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Only those who shoulder risks are qualified to welcome in the turning of the tide. Those who flee when troubles come are nothing more than deserters...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Though I shan't deny that I have your fortuitous arrival, and most outstanding assistance, to thank for my continued ability to speak such platitudes.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Either way, it seems this fragment is now utterly still. That must have made it useless to Rerir — I doubt he would have retreated so readily otherwise.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I imagine this wasn't the only reason you came looking for me, though...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, well, no, but...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly tell Flins about Rerir's murder of Sousi, and about the subsequent attempt to frame him.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah... I see.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can you think of a reason why Rerir would try to frame you?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: To use the Lightkeepers to find me, I suspect. I did not inform anyone of my true whereabouts, so he should have had more difficulty tracking me down.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: They alone have the ability to quickly pinpoint my position. Our Sergeant Major has a kuuvahki-powered device that can be used to detect others who bear a lantern.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: They usually don't pay my whereabouts much mind, unless they absolutely must find me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, you mean this thing?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Yes. Where did you pick this up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We found it inside a lantern when we first charged into the Wild Hunt anomaly.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It must belong to a Ratnik dispatched to investigate the area... who, it seems, dropped everything and fled the moment they saw the Wild Hunt massing to strike. Well, at least they're not dead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess it's not surprising how they found you so fast, then. But... If Rerir could've shapeshifted into Sousi, why didn't he just use that kuuvahki device to find you himself?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Were he to use it, that device would likely fail to act as it should — owing to Abyssal interference.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhh, guess that explains it...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So... Not only is this Rerir ruthless, but a purveyor of dirty tricks too.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You might not be familiar with Sergeant Major Sousi, but he put his heart and soul into every mission.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Our deployments are subject to orders from headquarters, and his orders were to be stationed long-term in Nasha Town. As such, he was very seldom able to go back and visit his family.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: He worked so, so hard, seeking to produce excellent results that might convince them to transfer him out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But every year, they would say, "Wait a little longer." "Wait a little longer." He often wondered if it was because he was lacking somehow.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In truth, everyone had nothing but the highest praise for him. But good work does not always lead to good outcomes.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The higher-ups would think, "He's doing great where he is. Let him stay there forever." A most convenient choice, for them at least.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Whereas his subordinates would think, "Wouldn't it be a shame if we were to lose such a talented, easygoing boss?"

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So he waited, and he waited. Until the world closed its eyes in the depths of the night, and a lantern was slowly lit for him alone, that no one could see.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a tragic story.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: One that has played out many times throughout history.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: ...Another reason to take this Rerir's head.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* At least we now know that he's looking for these fragments inside Wild Hunt anomalies...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And yet, what did the Sergeant Major have to do with any of this? Why did he have to die?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could Rerir be angry that the cannon Sousi set up to fire destroyed the fragments he wanted to collect?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hmm... Could you take me to the scene of the crime?

choices.text: Probably...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We shall just have to exercise some discretion, then. Come on, let us be on our way.

choices.text: ...But you are a suspect in this case.
Probably not.
...Why carry it on your person?

talks.objective: Return to the crime scene in Nasha Town

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I understand the situation, more or less. Much has happened, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Either way, I suppose we were lucky not to receive a "warm welcome" on the way over here. It seems my fellow Lightkeepers do not wish to make this case public just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Guess Nasha Town's already been enough of a mess lately.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Let's stop here. Any further, and the Ratniki might detect us.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Since you two can enter, I'll have to request that you kindly "pick me up" once you're inside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? And how are we supposed to do that...?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You'll know when the time comes. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, still acting all mysterious... But he seemed pretty confident, so guess we gotta trust him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Hello...

dialogues.speaker: Zvoni
dialogues.text: Ah, you're the special assistants for this investigation, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that's us.

choices.text: Sorry, I know it's a bit late...

response.speaker: Zvoni
response.text: Well, you're just in time. We're basically done investigating the crime scene. All that's left is to finish writing up some records, then properly dispose of Sergeant Major Sousi's remains.

response.speaker: Zvoni
response.text: If there's anything else you'd like to look into, this is your last chance to do so.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Find anything new?

response.speaker: Zvoni
response.text: Sadly, no. The motive behind the killing remains a mystery, and while we somehow managed to get news of Flins, an unexpected accident caused us to miss him.

response.speaker: Zvoni
response.text: But considering that Nefer from the Curatorium of Secrets came forward to help investigate, I have no doubt that a breakthrough's not far off.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Expert use of delaying tactics on her part. Excellent work...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll do our part too! Alright, we're going in. Seeya later!

choices.text: But there's a couple of things we'd like to take a look at.

talks.objective: Investigate once again

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we're in — thanks to Nefer's reputation, once again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we still know nothing about how Flins is gonna enter, or how we'll pick him up... never mind how we'll leave later on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Is something the matter, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a strange light by the window.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that looks like Flins's lantern... But where is he, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we've got the lantern. What now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waa— Ergh, Paimon almost screamed out loud! You never said you could do magic like that!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now that's what I call going incognito.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: This lantern may have a rather peculiar shape, but so long as it doesn't glow, it won't stand out in the dark.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I calculated that you would have already entered, so I chose a spot visible from the window before using light to send you a signal.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: As I thought, you're both sharp-eyed and on the ball.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, the perks of being veteran adventurers, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What you just did... Surely that can't be accomplished through elemental power alone?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Your composure is more impressive still. You're right. That required a little... trick of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But let us leave such trivial topics for a more relaxed moment. Our time is limited, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm. Just as I thought... Come, try sensing it yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's very faint, but there is some residual power near the wound that feels identical to the Abyssal energy that surged from Flins's lantern.)

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Identical powers must flow from the same source. It was the Wild Hunt, then, that took my form and killed the Sergeant Major... but why do this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To sow chaos by depriving the Lightkeepers of one of their commanders?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: If the Wild Hunt's true form is powerful enough to stand against the world as you claim, I fear not even the full force of Lightkeepers could stand against him, let alone the handful of us stationed in Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: He would have no reason whatsoever to pick quarrels with individual "ants."

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Let's look again more closely. We must leave no stone unturned.

choices.text: They said that the crime scene investigation is already complete.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, that makes things simpler. In that case, allow me to disturb the fallen. May the ghost-flame guide your spirit, may you rest in peace...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: However, despite a very thorough search, few new clues emerge.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: When we fought, he seemed like quite a reckless foe — certainly not the meticulous mastermind type. Yet here we are, grappling with this enigma he has left us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we can't get any leads, we might have to go back and find Nefer...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, the longer we're stuck here, the likelier he is to achieve his goal... This is so frustrating.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Is that all? Have we really tried every angle, found every clue?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, look at the flashing light on his arm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean this...?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I'm not well-versed in machinery... but that means his mechanical arm is malfunctioning, right? It might have been broken in combat...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that's not right. Paimon remembers this signal. We saw it before while repairing the cannon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It doesn't mean that the components are damaged. It just means that they're due for regular maintenance, so the device has stopped operating...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the real problem is that—

choices.text: When we were fixing the cannon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... He even helped us find the maintenance port!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It could still be a coincidence, but considering it hasn't been long at all since we were repairing that cannon...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: ...The Sousi you met could have been Rerir in disguise. In other words, he played the Sergeant Major before disguising himself as me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! If only there was some way to prove it...

choices.text: If something needed maintenance...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You mean Hintsa?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We had a short chat with him once at the tavern, but it's so late... Guess it'll have to wait till tomorrow.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I know where he lives. The situation is critical, so let us now take up the role of uninvited guests ourselves.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, yes, and one more thing...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Remember to "pick me up" by the window.

choices.text: You'd go register it with Nasha Town's repairman.
...His arm was working just fine.
There should no longer be a need to keep this place exactly as-is.

talks.objective: Look for Hintsa and ask about the situation

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: *yawn* ...Ah, it's you two... and Flins. Given the hour, I guess it must be an emergency?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It is indeed. Our sincerest apologies for interrupting your rest.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We're investigating a certain matter in connection with Sergeant Major Sousi. We'd like to know if he has sent you a request for maintenance to be performed on his mechanical arm.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Sousi... Oh. So the rumors I heard... are they true?

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: *sigh*... You know what? Forget it... I'm sure it's complicated. No further questions from me. Just a moment — I need to check my records.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Thank you for your understanding.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Got it. Eight days ago, he came to request a round of regular maintenance, but as it happened, I had run out of the required components.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: His mechanical arm is especially sophisticated, having been designed by Aino personally. The parts, too, could only be made by her.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: As such, they usually take several days to arrive. In fact, this time, he even asked me if we could push his request forward.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: And I understood, completely. Not being able to use your hand... That's rough for anyone, but even more so if your job involves fighting out in the wild. So I did my best to convince Aino to rush the job...

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: And eventually, the parts arrived — three days ago, if I remember correctly. I sent word to the Lightkeepers immediately, but he never showed up. I assumed he was just out on some mission or other...

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Uh... What's with those faces? Everything alright?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You've provided us with some very crucial information, Hintsa. You have our thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We can't make everything public yet, but once our investigation is complete, I will return to thank you and provide an explanation on behalf of all the Lightkeepers.

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: No worries. Just glad I could help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks. Good night!

dialogues.speaker: Hintsa
dialogues.text: Good night. Hope the investigation goes well.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It seems that it is as we guessed. The "Sergeant Major Sousi" you encountered while repairing the cannon was actually Rerir in disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Eight days ago, he had yet to act, but at some point after that, he attacked and imprisoned the Sergeant Major.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: With the immense gap in strength between them, the job was finished in a single blow — and thus, Rerir had no opportunity to discover the malfunctioning mechanical arm.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Perhaps his mastery of shapeshifting extends only to outward form — and not, therefore, to complex internal mechanisms. Hence his oversight of the uniquely mechanical traits of the Sergeant Major's arm, and in turn, this flaw in his disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're saying he thought no one would realize his mechanical arm was actually made of some kinda black muck on the inside, so long as it worked, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Still seems like there's a lot of guesswork involved here, but it mostly makes sense...

choices.text: That means that the only thing he did as Sousi...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: This also has me stumped for the moment. The cannon has always been used to destroy the Wild Hunt, and it works as intended.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But how would that help Rerir, exactly...?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Assuming he plans to collect the fragments within Wild Hunt anomalies, firing the cannon works against him, since it would blast those fragments to smithereens.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, so we solved one mystery only to dig up another...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is getting Paimon kinda down... *yawn* and sleepy, too...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've been on edge for too long, it seems.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Yes, I'd say it is high time we took a break. Seems like there's a lot left to investigate.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We'll have to fight Rerir eventually — and we'll do a poor job if we're not well-rested.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we should totally get some sleep first...

choices.text: Want to rest a day in Nasha Town?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: A reasonable suggestion. I have no doubt that my quarters have been turned inside out by now, at any rate.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: My colleagues have never failed to live up to my expectations of their discourtesy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, guess we'll just have to "pick you up" as usual...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: That would be good, yes. Feel free to put the room costs on my tab.

choices.text: Your residence is quite far away.
...Was fire the cannon.

talks.objective: Bring Flins back to The Flagship to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, back inside! We can finally take a breather! Okay, Paimon, in and out!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Haha, I suppose we could all take a moment to unwind. Hmm, as I recall, our first meeting took place not far from here. Ah, the nostalgia.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Had you already sensed the unique power within my lantern at that time?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, which is why I asked you to give it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I see. Ah, words truly do fail to capture your superlative insight.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Fortunate, then, that Abyssal energy was only leaking from the fragment in miniscule amounts when we first met, or I might have been in for a real interrogation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Hard to say how that would've played out. We've had a whole bunch of unpleasant run-ins with the Abyss...

choices.text: Rerir seems fixated on you...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You mean to ask why I'm going this far to oppose him? Well, as a Lightkeeper, I'd say I'm simply doing my job.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Come on, don't play games with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You're covered in more mysteries than Paimon could shake a skewer at. You can't just get out of explaining yourself by making lame excuses!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hmm, alright. I suppose I do owe you some honesty, whether out of gratitude or the need to build trust.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Your deductions have been quite correct. Should one wish to conceal oneself within a lantern, elemental power alone is not enough.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You know humans well, and naturally, you understand their limits.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But some things that humans would consider difficult are quite normal in the eyes of non-humans.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you mean you're one of the latter?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Have you heard of how Snezhnaya was once the realm of the fae?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: This race is no longer of any importance, but they still exist — as evidenced by the fact that I am standing before you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've heard some scattered legends, but... that's all Paimon thought there was to it.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I once turned my heart toward humanity, and thus did I experience loss. I once labored and did much, and put an end to my tale with my own hands.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: When you realize you are floating in the middle of a vast ocean, you cannot help but feel that swimming in any direction would be equally meaningless.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Would it not be better, then, to simply sink?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But before I could sink to truly lightless depths, chance had it that I should be awakened by a band of Ratniki.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: They were facing a horde of Abyssal monsters, and could not last against such a disparity in strength, yet none fled.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Those who dwell in darkness for long enough become exceedingly sensitive to all light — and the first light I saw upon awakening was that which shone from their eyes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that why you chose to help them?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Perhaps I was moved by their valor. Perhaps I simply saw my past self in them, and was moved to action for the first time in a long, long while.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But I was freshly awoken, and my powers were limited. I could not prevent casualties altogether.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The survivors and I buried the fallen heroes... That was the origin of the "Final Night Cemetery."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And that's why you chose to become a Lightkeeper...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, not exactly. I was just more familiar with them, so joining up seemed the most convenient way to experience human life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Doesn't sound too believable...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, I believe it. Besides, I'm well past the age when one might believe in "things that must be done."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Nonetheless, there are still some things I will not allow to happen. The chaos that Rerir has been stirring up is one of them.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Tomorrow, I shall go and check our records to see if I can find any connection between the Wild Hunt, Rerir, and the cannon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will you need us to get you where you need to be?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Oh, I'll be fine. I keep a backup copy at my residence in case of emergencies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can... you even go back there right now? Won't there be Ratniki watching it?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Thanks for the reminder. I believe they'll have checked my place, but they won't have stayed. All things are ranked according to their priority, and we lack the manpower for such an open-ended stakeout.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And even if someone is waiting, I have ways around that. I am the master of my own house, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then, we'll trust you. *yawn* We sure ended up chatting for a while, huh? Paimon's super tired now, but... Y'know, feels like we can breathe easier, now that we know you better.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Haha. I didn't take you for the cautious sort.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Anyway, I hope you'll help me keep this a secret. I'd prefer others not to know about my past unless strictly necessary, nor do I want to attract more trouble on account of being a fae.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I won't say a thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's lips are sealed too!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Alright. Thanks again for your help. Good night, you two.

choices.text: ...And you, on him.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hang on. Weren't you supposed to bring me some candy? You said you would!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, sorry, but things happened kinda suddenly, so—

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You leave the room without any trouble, and start heading toward Hintsa's residence.
